\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا} (dākhil karnā)}{داخل کرنا (dākhil karnā)}]{\ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا} (dākhil karnā) — to admit to hospital}

\label{lesson:UR-C479-dakhil-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for pus, then the Urdu for to pick at.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{dākhil karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to admit to hospital\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ڈاکٹروں} \ur{نے} \ur{دادا} \ur{کو} \ur{ہسپتال} \ur{میں} \ur{داخل} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍākṭaroṅ ne dādā ko haspatāl meṅ dākhil kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctors admitted my grandfather to hospital.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کو} \ur{داخل} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne marīz ko dākhil kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{dākhil karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{داخل}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dākhil}, \textquotedblleft{}entering\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dākhil karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dākhil karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭaroṅ ne dādā ko haspatāl meṅ dākhil kiyā.} — The doctors admitted my grandfather to hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for pus, then the Urdu for to pick at, then say \emph{dākhil karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To admit to hospital\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{وارڈ} (vārḍ)}{وارڈ (vārḍ)}]{\ur{وارڈ} (vārḍ) — a hospital ward}

\label{lesson:UR-C479-vard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pick at, then the Urdu for to admit to hospital.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{وارڈ}}
\textbf{\ur{وارڈ}} — \emph{vārḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}a hospital ward\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مریض} \ur{اوپر} \ur{والے} \ur{وارڈ} \ur{میں} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{marīz ūpar vāle vārḍ meṅ hai.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سرجن} (sarjan)}{سرجن (sarjan)}]{\ur{سرجن} (sarjan) — a surgeon}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from An Upset Stomach to In Hospital}

\label{lesson:UR-R479-review-472-479}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for to digest and digestion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to digest, digestion, indigestion, retching, nourishment
  \item to ache dully, a cramp, to grip tight, to limp, an inflammation
  \item germs, contagious, an infection, measles, smallpox
  \item chronic, asthma, paralysis, cancer, afflicted
  \item to examine, a medical test, a diagnosis, a traditional physician, to have (someone) sent for
  \item a droplet, to dissolve, a capsule, a paper packet, to toss into the mouth
  \item to prick, an incision, a stitch, pus, to pick at
  \item to admit to hospital, a hospital ward, an operation, a surgeon, a stretcher
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To digest? (\textbf{\ur{ہضم} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{hazm karnā}.) Digestion? (\textbf{\ur{ہاضمہ}}, \emph{hāzmā}.) Indigestion? (\textbf{\ur{بدہضمی}}, \emph{badhazmī}.) Retching? (\textbf{\ur{ابکائی}}, \emph{ubkāī}.) Nourishment? (\textbf{\ur{غذا}}, \emph{ghizā}.) To ache dully? (\textbf{\ur{کسکنا}}, \emph{kasaknā}.) A cramp? (\textbf{\ur{اینٹھن}}, \emph{aiṅṭhan}.) To grip tight? (\textbf{\ur{جکڑنا}}, \emph{jakaṛnā}.) To limp? (\textbf{\ur{لنگڑانا}}, \emph{laṅgṛānā}.) An inflammation? (\textbf{\ur{سوزش}}, \emph{sozish}.) Germs? (\textbf{\ur{جراثیم}}, \emph{jarāsīm}.) Contagious? (\textbf{\ur{متعدی}}, \emph{mutāddī}.) An infection? (\textbf{\ur{انفیکشن}}, \emph{infekshan}.) Measles? (\textbf{\ur{خسرہ}}, \emph{khasrā}.) Smallpox? (\textbf{\ur{چیچک}}, \emph{chechak}.) Chronic? (\textbf{\ur{دائمی}}, \emph{dāimī}.) Asthma? (\textbf{\ur{دمہ}}, \emph{damā}.) Paralysis? (\textbf{\ur{فالج}}, \emph{fālij}.) Cancer? (\textbf{\ur{کینسر}}, \emph{kainsar}.) Afflicted? (\textbf{\ur{مبتلا}}, \emph{mubtalā}.) To examine? (\textbf{\ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{muāinā karnā}.) A medical test? (\textbf{\ur{ٹیسٹ}}, \emph{ṭesṭ}.) A diagnosis? (\textbf{\ur{تشخیص}}, \emph{tashkhīs}.) A traditional physician? (\textbf{\ur{حکیم}}, \emph{hakīm}.) To have (someone) sent for? (\textbf{\ur{بلوانا}}, \emph{bulvānā}.) A droplet? (\textbf{\ur{قطرہ}}, \emph{qatrā}.) To dissolve? (\textbf{\ur{گھولنا}}, \emph{gholnā}.) A capsule? (\textbf{\ur{کیپسول}}, \emph{kaipsūl}.) A paper packet? (\textbf{\ur{پڑیا}}, \emph{puṛiyā}.) To toss into the mouth? (\textbf{\ur{پھانکنا}}, \emph{phāṅknā}.) To prick? (\textbf{\ur{چبھنا}}, \emph{chubhnā}.) An incision? (\textbf{\ur{چیرا}}, \emph{chīrā}.) A stitch? (\textbf{\ur{ٹانکا}}, \emph{ṭāṅkā}.) Pus? (\textbf{\ur{پیپ}}, \emph{pīp}.) To pick at? (\textbf{\ur{کریدنا}}, \emph{kurednā}.) To admit to hospital? (\textbf{\ur{داخل} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{dākhil karnā}.) A hospital ward? (\textbf{\ur{وارڈ}}, \emph{vārḍ}.) An operation? (\textbf{\ur{آپریشن}}, \emph{āpreshan}.) A surgeon? (\textbf{\ur{سرجن}}, \emph{sarjan}.) A stretcher? (\textbf{\ur{اسٹریچر}}, \emph{isṭrechar}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
